claims: A major is a senior military officer (O-4) in the US Army, Air Force, or Marines.
A major ranks below lieutenant colonel.
Majors earn roughly $7,000–$12,000+ monthly based on experience.
Majors act as primary staff officers or company commanders.
An academic major is a student's specialized college field.
Military majors (O-4) are key staff officers for brigade-level planning.
Military majors (O-4) are Executive Officers (XO) in battalions.
Becoming a military major requires a bachelor's degree.
Becoming a military major requires completion of officer candidate/training school.
Becoming a military major requires several years of service as a commissioned officer.
Salary for military majors (O-4) depends on pay grade (O-4) and years of service.
Salary for military majors (O-4) includes Basic Pay + Allowances for Housing/Subsistence.
An academic major is the primary subject area a college student chooses to specialize in.
An academic major comprises one-third to one-half of their coursework.
Examples of academic major types include arts/humanities (literature, art), business (finance, marketing), health/medicine, and sciences.
"Major" refers to a person of legal age.
In music, a major is a scale or key with specific intervals.
